A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same causal concept faithfulness research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched reliably, including the additional material in v2.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A, D, and E report original LLM experiments, faithfulness estimates, intervention results, and supplementary analyses on social bias and medical question answering.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports manual audits of extracted concepts and generated counterfactuals in Appendix F.3.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 and Appendix C retain the same concept extraction, counterfactual generation, explanation analysis, and Bayesian hierarchical estimation procedures. Appendix F.3 audits these components without introducing a method modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same BBQ social bias and MedQA medical question-answering coverage, including the existing appendix scenarios. The new audits inspect outputs from these experiments without adding datasets or task conditions.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparison method is added or removed. The same LLM evaluations and standard versus anti-bias prompt comparisons remain; the expanded discussion of Siegel et al. is not an experimental baseline comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix F.3 adds a manual audit protocol using 15 randomly sampled questions and 50 counterfactuals per dataset. It specifies concept-validity and disentanglement criteria, plus counterfactual coherency, completeness, and minimality criteria. The original faithfulness evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused error analysis of auxiliary concept extraction and counterfactual generation, with audited frequencies and annotated cases in Tables 37–40. This extends v1's isolated error discussion and example outputs; the existing robustness, prompting, and question-level analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The Bayesian 90% credible intervals and Appendix D.4's 1,000-bootstrap procedure are unchanged. The new audit reports counts and percentages without adding uncertainty estimates, repeated-run information, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Appendix F.3 newly reports entangled concepts in two of 15 audited questions for each dataset, while all inspected concepts satisfy referential validity. Counterfactual error rates are 6% for BBQ and 10% for MedQA, each based on 50 inspected counterfactuals. Existing faithfulness scores, rankings, and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions 2.1–2.3, the causal assumptions and derivations in Appendix B, and the hierarchical models in Appendix C are unchanged. The new audit criteria and failure explanations do not revise the formal mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about defining and estimating causal concept faithfulness and identifying semantic patterns of unfaithfulness. The audit supplies additional evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F.3 explains how entangled concepts produce redundant interventions and how faulty counterfactuals could affect dataset-level faithfulness. It argues that these effects should be small and identifies possible future remedies, extending v1's general error caveat and correlated-concept discussion.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses that counterfactuals associated with every presented question-level result were manually checked for errors affecting interpretation. Appendix F.3 also documents the audit criteria and sampling. Existing prompts, model versions, generation parameters, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 expands its treatment of the already-cited Siegel et al. (2024), explicitly relating intervention-impact and explanation-mention scores to CE and EE and explaining inherited limitations from Atanasova et al. The cited-work set remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendix F.3 and makes localized edits to related work, limitations, cross-references, and the Figure 3 caption. The main narrative and existing section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Tables 37–40 add displays of entangled concepts and erroneous counterfactuals using bold and colored annotations. Some material is redisplayed, including the BBQ edit from Table 33 in Table 39. Figure 3's caption is shortened, while the existing plots and original table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix F.3 and Tables 37–40 make previously scattered concerns about auxiliary-LLM reliability more assessable through explicit audit criteria, error frequencies, and examples. The clearer comparison with Siegel et al. also improves positioning. These are useful but limited gains: v2 does not quantify how the identified errors affect the retained faithfulness estimates.
